name: Token
statusNote: Alpha in Primer React, accessibility-reviewed 2025-01-08. It ships inside TextInputWithTokens and Autocomplete across GitHub. Its hover style is dead code (see notes), so the shipped look has no hover change on a plain Token.
summary: A compact pill for one selected value (a user, a label, a filter) that may be clickable, selectable and removable. Choose it over Label when the user acts on the value; use IssueLabelToken, its sibling, when the value is a GitHub label with an arbitrary colour.

inputs.name: leadingVisual
inputs.description: A visual before the text (an avatar or icon); not rendered at small. Token only, not IssueLabelToken.

inputs.name: onRemove
inputs.description: Called by the remove button and by Backspace or Delete while the token has focus. Its presence adds the remove button.

inputs.name: hideRemoveButton
inputs.description: Keep keyboard removal but draw no remove button.

inputs.name: isSelected
inputs.description: Draw the selected state (e.g. the token the caret is on inside a token input).

inputs.name: disabled
inputs.description: Not interactive: the cursor stays default and the remove button is a real button again. There is no disabled colour.

inputs.name: fillColor
inputs.description: IssueLabelToken only: the label's colour as any CSS colour; every colour of the token is derived from it.

anatomy.name: Container
anatomy.description: A full-radius pill with a 1px border, height by size, semibold text with no wrap. Positioned, so the text's hit overlay can cover it.

anatomy.name: Leading visual
anatomy.description: Token only, medium and up: a non-shrinking visual 4px (6px at large and xlarge) before the text.

anatomy.name: Text
anatomy.description: The label, one line, ellipsized when the token is narrower than its text; grows to fill the token. When the token has both a click target and a remove button, this part is the link or button and its hit area covers the whole token.

anatomy.name: Remove button
anatomy.description: A round, square-sized hit target as tall as the token, holding a 12px X (16px at large and xlarge); the token's end padding drops to 0 to make room.

anatomy.name: Selection ring
anatomy.description: IssueLabelToken only: a 2px ring 2px outside the pill while selected, in a colour derived from fillColor.

variants.description: Neutral muted fill, muted text and border.
Every colour derived at run time from fillColor (see the colour rules); no leading visual and no screen-reader removal hint.
16px tall, 4px side padding, small body text; no leading visual; 16px remove target with a 12px X.
20px tall, 6px side padding, small body text; 20px remove target with a 12px X.
24px tall, 8px side padding, medium body text; 24px remove target with a 16px X, 6px before it.
32px tall, 12px side padding, medium body text; 32px remove target with a 16px X, 6px before it.

layout.text: Height is the size's base size exactly: --base-size-16, --base-size-20, --base-size-24 or --base-size-32 (16, 20, 24, 32px), border included; side padding --base-size-4, -6, -8 or -12; text --text-body-size-small at small and medium, --text-body-size-medium at large and xlarge.
The container is an inline row centred on its cross axis, max-width 100% of its parent; the text part takes the remaining width (flex-grow 1, min-width 0), clips and ends in an ellipsis.
Token's border is 1px solid, set as an inline style; IssueLabelToken's is --borderWidth-thin solid.
The leading visual sits 4px before the text (6px at large and xlarge), with line height 0 so it adds no height, and never shrinks; small tokens drop it.

With a remove button the token's end padding is 0; the button is a square of the token's height with a full radius, 4px after the text (6px at large and xlarge), its X 12px at small and medium and 16px at large and xlarge, baseline-aligned and translated 1px right and 1px up (the border width) so it sits on the pill's outer edge.

states.text: Token: --fgColor-muted text on --bgColor-neutral-muted with a --borderColor-muted border. The cursor is a pointer only when the token is interactive.

Token: the module defines a hover of --fgColor-default text and a --shadow-resting-medium lift for [data-interactive=true], but Token never sets that attribute, so a plain Token shows no hover change. IssueLabelToken does change on hover when interactive (see the colour rules).
Token: --fgColor-default text and a --borderColor-emphasis border. IssueLabelToken: a darker fill (light) and a 2px ring 2px outside the pill.
The remove button fills with --control-transparent-bgColor-hover on hover and on focus, and --control-transparent-bgColor-active while pressed.
disabled only removes interactivity (default cursor, no click target); no colour changes.

behaviour.text: A token is interactive when it is not disabled and has onClick, onFocus, a tabIndex of 0 or more, or is rendered as a link or button.

Interactive without a remove button: the whole pill is the link or button. Interactive with a visible remove button (two action targets): the text part becomes the link or button and stretches an invisible hit area over the whole pill, while the remove button stays on top of it and takes its own clicks; a remove click does not reach the token.
Backspace or Delete while focus is in the token calls onRemove, after any caller key handler; this works with the remove button hidden.

With two action targets the remove control is not focusable (tabIndex -1) and hidden from assistive technology; removal is by Backspace or Delete on the focused text target. Otherwise the remove control is a real button named "Remove token" in the tab order.

IssueLabelToken colour, inputs: parse fillColor to r, g, b (0-255) and to h (degrees), s and l (percent), each rounded to an integer; perceived lightness P = (0.2126 r + 0.7152 g + 0.0722 b) / 255 (no gamma linearisation); switch = clamp(1 / (T - P), 0, 1), which is 1 when P < T and 0 when P > T, where T depends on the theme family below.

IssueLabelToken, light themes (T = 0.453): fill rgb(r, g, b); text white when switch is 1, black when 0; border hsla(h, s, l - 25, a) with a = clamp((P - 0.96) * 100, 0, 1), so only near-white labels get a visible border. Selected: fill hsl(h, s, l - 5) and a 2px ring of rgb(r, g, b). Interactive hover: a 15% black layer over the fill plus --shadow-resting-medium.

IssueLabelToken, dark themes (T = 0.6): lightenBy = (0.6 - P) * 100 * switch; fill rgba(r, g, b, 0.18); text hsl(h, s, l + lightenBy); border the text colour at alpha 0.3. Selected: a 2px ring in the text colour. Interactive hover: fill hsla(h, s, l + 10, 0.3) plus --shadow-resting-medium.

IssueLabelToken picks the light or dark formula by the active theme's family (its name contains light or dark), honouring the colour mode and, in auto mode, the system preference; high-contrast, colorblind and tritanopia themes use their family's formula unchanged.

accessibility.role: button or link when interactive, else none (a generic span)
keyboard: Tab focuses an interactive token (or its text target).
Enter activates a link token; Enter or Space a button token.
Backspace or Delete removes the focused token when onRemove is set.
semantics: Token with onRemove appends visually hidden text " (press backspace or delete to remove)" to its name; IssueLabelToken does not.
The standalone remove button is named "Remove token"; the in-token remove control with two targets is aria-hidden.
isSelected has no ARIA counterpart here; the containing widget must expose selection.

notes.text: Token.module.css styles hover on [data-interactive='true'], but Token sets data-cursor-is-interactive, never data-interactive, so the hover text colour and shadow never apply.

No module draws a focus ring for the token, its text target or the remove button; the browser's default focus outline is what users see. A native build must draw one; the foundations' 2px --focus-outline-color outline is the consistent choice.
The text ellipsis is CSS text-overflow; a native build must measure the text and truncate it to the width left after padding, leading visual and remove button.

IssueLabelToken's colours are CSS calc() over custom properties evaluated per frame; a native build computes them once per fillColor and theme family with the formulas above, clamping each HSL lightness to 0-100%.
At exactly P = T the switch divides by zero; CSS resolves 1/0 to infinity and clamps it to 1 (white text in light). Guard the division.
The remove target is the token's full height, so it overhangs the 1px border by the translate; it is the only sub-part with hover and press colours.
